proofs.full_local_argument: Write e_k=V_k-B(x_k), D_{k,j}=B_{I_{k,j}}(x_k)-B_{I_{k,j}}(x_{k-1}), and mu_k=B(x_k)-B(x_{k-1}). Given F_{k-1}, both points and e_{k-1} are fixed, and the D_{k,j} are iid with conditional mean mu_k. Define z_k=S^{-1}sum_j(D_{k,j}-mu_k). Thus E[z_k|F_{k-1}]=0 and e_k=e_{k-1}+z_k. The finite conditional second moment is bounded by the assumed mean-square Lipschitz inequality. Conditional independence and zero means give E[||z_k||^2|F_{k-1}]=S^{-1}E[||D_{k,1}-mu_k||^2|F_{k-1}]=S^{-1}(E[||D_{k,1}||^2|F_{k-1}]-||mu_k||^2)<=L_B^2||x_k-x_{k-1}||^2/S<=L_B^2 epsilon_1^2/S. Starting from square-integrable e_0, induction shows each e_k is square-integrable. Since e_{k-1} is F_{k-1}-measurable, E[<e_{k-1},z_k>|F_{k-1}]=0. Expanding the square therefore gives E[||e_k||^2|F_{k-1}]=||e_{k-1}||^2+E[||z_k||^2|F_{k-1}]<=||e_{k-1}||^2+L_B^2 epsilon_1^2/S. Taking expectations and iterating k times proves the stated bound, including equality of the bound with the initial error at k=0. This argument uses square integrability of errors and increments; separate square integrability of B(x_0) is unnecessary.

assumptions: For every x,y in R^d, n^{-1}sum_i ||B_i(x)-B_i(y)||^2 <= L_B^2||x-y||^2.
E||V_0-B(x_0)||^2 is finite; V_{k-1} and x_{k-1} are measurable with respect to F_{k-1}.
The same sampled index is reused at the two evaluation points within each summand. Each round uses a fresh iid with-replacement batch independent of the complete pre-draw history.
statement.conclusion: For every k=0,...,K, E||V_k-B(x_k)||^2 <= E||V_0-B(x_0)||^2 + k L_B^2 epsilon_1^2/S.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let n,d,m,S,K be positive integers. Let B_i:R^d->R^m, i in [n], be deterministic measurable maps and B(x)=n^{-1}sum_{i=1}^n B_i(x); all vector norms are Euclidean. Let (F_k)_{k=0}^K be a filtration. Let x_0,V_0 be F_0-measurable and x_k be F_{k-1}-measurable for 1<=k<=K. At round k, draw I_{k,1},...,I_{k,S} independently and uniformly from [n], jointly independent of F_{k-1}, and include these draws in F_k. Set V_k=V_{k-1}+S^{-1}sum_{j=1}^S[B_{I_{k,j}}(x_k)-B_{I_{k,j}}(x_{k-1})].
statement.parameter_domains: n,d,m,S,K in positive integers; L_B,epsilon_1 finite nonnegative real numbers. No convexity, gradient structure or objective-function assumption is required.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every choice of the displayed maps, filtration, initialization and predictable path satisfying these conditions, simultaneously as deterministic expectation inequalities for each k=0,...,K, the conclusion holds. Expectations include initialization, path and all batch randomness. No simultaneous high-probability assertion is made.
